subject: survival in MARK - incomplete capture history

messages.author: 39971e2c19b8ec70
messages.subject: survival in MARK - incomplete capture history
parts:
Hi all!

I am producing survival estimates from Constant Effort Sites data using MARK.
I used dot for the missing visits in capture history:

1892 0000001000. 1
1893 ....001.... 1
1894 ....001.... 1
1895 ....001.... 1
1896 ....001.... 1
1897 ....001.... 1
1898 ....001.... 1
1899 .....100000 1
1900 .....100000 1

However, now I found that programs for GOF tests - RELEASE and U-CARE - are
not working with this data at all. I've been told by Olivier that this is
kind of non-standard and he seemed surprised that MARK allows this. But how else
would you specify a missing visit (NA)? Seems quite a common situation in
real life data.

So I have two questions:

1) How can I specify missing visits to MARK? Does it work with the dot? I
was using it like this and supposed it works but now when I look in the MARK
book (http://www.phidot.org/software/mark/docs/book/), the only
documentation available, it is not mentioned there!

2) Are there any ways how to run GOF tests on data with missing visits?

Thanks a lot,

Tomas

PS: I am using newest versions of RMark R package for RELEASE and R2ucare for U-CARE in R.

messages.author: 0216939e087e502c
messages.subject: Re: survival in MARK - incomplete capture history
parts:
Dear Tomas,


I believe that you can discard the capture histories like the one in the 2nd row. I think they are like a caphist with a one in the very last occasion; they don't contain any extractable info about survival via de CJS model.


Otherwise, why don't you aggregate the data to the m-array and then run a Bayesian posterior predictive check ? That's perhaps not as good as the diagnostic checks in RELEASE (because it doesn't tell you in which way the data are problematic), but at least it's somehting.


best regards  ---- Marc
